reviewedRevision: 2c81d920 (accepted build) plus the fixes in this commit
reviewer: phase-fair, phase-robust and phase-present (parallel split review)
process: Lean final review at the user's request, with the review split across three parallel reviewers (fairness, robustness, presentation) as the user asked. The game already had 26 boards; robustness passed outright. Three MEDIUM findings and two LOW items were fixed and verified by a separate verification agent re-running the reviewers' probes against the repository files (owner copies changed only to request the now opt-in hint) plus one clean-worktree run, then by the browser check, without a second review round.
independentProbes: On the final files the fairness reviewer's planning bot (public getState only, solving its own linear system) cleared all 26 boards at 0.25 s and 0.35 s with plan cost equal to the optimum; press slack now averages 1.75 on teaching boards, 1.00 on combination boards and 0.38 on mastery boards, with boards 20, 22, 23, 25 and 26 allowing no spare press. A bot that only follows the opt-in hint clears every board but finishes with 1,150 of 2,600 points, where the review had found the always-on hint solving every board for free. Blind policies cleared nothing from board 3, 40 scripted snapshots matched across 30, 60 and 120 Hz, 49 hostile-input cases produced no failures, endings and every broken progress store were safe, no soft-lock was found on any board, and EN and ZH text fits with no Latin in Chinese.

findings.observation: Fairness finding: the always-on hint named the next move, so following it solved every board at optimal presses. Boards 1-7 keep the step hint; from board 8 the line states the goal ('Match every tile to the target card [H] hint -10') and H or the Hint touch button reveals one move for 10 points; getState exposes the hint only while shown.
Fairness finding: every combination and mastery board allowed one spare press, so mastery was no tighter. Mastery boards 20, 22, 23, 25 and 26 now allow none, and every board remains solvable.
Presentation finding: the target card and each tile's ghost mark showed the target phase by colour alone. Both now draw the same phase bars as the tiles.
The undo hint marks the tile Z will undo with a pulsing frame and a Z badge, and arrows, WASD, Space, Enter or a tap skip the clear pause instead of being ignored.

openNotes: A player can still buy every hint; the cost is score, not progress.
Locked boards on the picker are shown dimmed without a padlock; the reviewer did not flag it, and the board number stays readable.

browser.method: Official Claude in Chrome extension, local server; real clicks on Start and the language toggle, synthetic in-page keys driven by the status line; only DOM text and the canvas were read.
observed: English: Start opened board 1 of 26 (First Stitch) with the shape preview, the phase legend and the target card, whose swatches now carry phase bars; the description explained that hints are bought with H from board 8.
Win: following the prompts pressed the right tiles, the board matched ('Board clear! Next board coming') and board 2 opened.
Chinese 390 px phone frame (388 px inner, no horizontal overflow): the board picker in Chinese with touch buttons 左, 右, 上, 下, 按下, 撤销, 重置 and 提示.
Not covered in the browser: a bought hint, a zero-slack board and a loss; the probes and quality tests cover them.
